subject: Pyrelands
advisory: A burned patch looks about a third green on day 3 and about 60% on day 7 (measured 26.2/59.8 against his 25/60 card thresholds); whether a week-old scar should look nearly all green is playtest tuning

leaves.oracle_proposed: fire-cell census per game hour shows a contiguous front whose centroid moves and a growing scorched area behind it; after the front dies, a relight is read within the smoulder window, in open grass beyond the building margin; captures of the front
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player, landing on a fresh Pyrelands map in ordinary play and watching at play zoom through the first days, sees a line of grass fire walking across the deep ash with a black scorched trail behind its front; when it dies down it is never out for long, a smoulder relighting in open grass far from buildings. It must not read as a scattered wildfire, a fire that burns once and is gone for good, or a front that lights inside the colony.
leaves.scenario: Generate a fresh Pyrelands map with its opening front; capture the front each game hour for a day; let it die down and wait for the smoulder relight; record each relight cell's distance from the nearest building.
false_pass: a fire spawned by the test where the front should be, so a burn exists but nothing walks
the opening front lights once and the map stays dark for good
leaves.red: the burn line lights on arrival and never relights after it goes out, so by day three the map holds no fire
leaves.owner_part: yes: the burn line walking across deep ash with its scorched trail

leaves.oracle_proposed: terrain census shows deep ash on most cells with soil and gravel as small pockets and richer ground next to water; captures show blowing ash in clear weather; loose-ash count rises each hour of ash fall and light level drops; loose ash on the burned pad after the fire, none beyond ambient drift with ash-dusting off
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player on a fresh Pyrelands map sees almost all the ground as deep ash with small pockets of unburned soil and gravel and richer ground ringing standing water, and in any weather a lot of free-blowing ash blowing across it like snow; during ash fall the map dims and loose-ash drifts keep banking, and a fire burning across deep ash leaves loose ash lying behind it. It must not read as ordinary soil with a grey tint, or as a clear sky with ash only on the ground.
leaves.scenario: Fresh map: terrain census over the whole map; capture open ground at play zoom in clear weather; force ash fall for half a day and count loose-ash filth and read the light level each hour. Separately, burn a grassed deep-ash pad in clear weather and count loose-ash filth on it after the fire, against the same burn with fire ash-dusting switched off.
false_pass: the census counts a deep-ash label laid over soil whose fertility is unchanged
the blowing ash is a weather overlay that only shows during ash fall
the loose ash on the burned pad is ambient drift that would have banked there without any fire
leaves.red: the map generates mostly soil with a few ash pockets, or no ash blows in clear weather, or a fire on deep ash leaves the ground clean

leaves.oracle_proposed: per-cell fertility reads about 140% beside water and about 40% dry; daily growth of the watered strip is clearly ahead
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player farming a strip of deep ash beside a watered channel sees the crop there grow clearly faster than the same crop on dry ash a few cells away. It must not read as ash being barren everywhere, or as ash being rich everywhere.
leaves.scenario: Two strips of the same crop sown on the same tick on deep ash, one beside water and one dry; read growth each day for five days.
false_pass: the watered strip is sown on soil rather than ash
both strips are on rich ground, so the gap is noise
leaves.red: deep ash beside water grows the crop no faster than dry deep ash

leaves.oracle_proposed: fertility reads about 190% on the wet fresh scar, about 90% on the dry fresh scar and about 140% on wet old ash while the rain lasts; the burn bonus falls to zero by day 6 to 7 on its own clock, rain or no rain
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player who sows on ground the fire has just crossed sees that crop grow noticeably faster for a few days than one sown on old ash; when black rain falls on the fresh scar the bonus is not washed away but adds to the watering, so a wet fresh scar out-grows both a dry fresh scar and wet old ash, and the bonus then fades on its own six-day clock. It must not read as black rain wiping the burn bonus, or as a bonus that never fades.
leaves.scenario: Three pads on deep ash: freshly burned, freshly burned then black rain for half a day, old ash under the same black rain; read fertility and crop growth on each through day 7.
false_pass: the rain pad's fertility is read before the rain falls
the burn bonus is read from a setting instead of the cell
leaves.red: black rain still wipes the burn bonus within half a day, so the rained-on fresh scar reads no better than wet old ash (the built behaviour before 2026-11-05)

leaves.oracle_proposed: cover census shows dense grass on open cells; green share at least 25% on day 3 and at least 60% on day 7 (his card thresholds); captures show the greening
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player sees open ground carpeted thick in ember grass with no bare-dirt expanses, and a burned patch of it visibly re-greening within a few days and largely green again within about a week at the biome's own heat. It must not read as a scar that stays black for a season, or as grass that is green the moment the fire passes.
leaves.scenario: Fresh map: grass cover census on open cells; burn a patch of ember grass on deep ash; capture and count green cells on days 1, 3 and 7.
false_pass: the regrowth is read on a patch the test replanted
the cover census counts grass on cells the density enforcer just filled for the test
leaves.red: a burned patch stays mostly black after a week, or open ground shows wide bare dirt

leaves.oracle_proposed: count on the burned pad above zero within the burn itself (pods roll on the burning cell's fire tick) and on the unburned pad zero from a map-wide zero start; harvest yields fruit and the eater's food need rises; the unpicked plant is gone within about a day and the stack rots within about four days
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player watching the burn line pass sees scorch-fruit come up rapidly in the fresh scar right behind the front, while the ground is still smoking, and never on unburned ground; it ripens to fruit a colonist can pick and eat to feed, and rots fast: a ripe plant withers within about a day and picked fruit rots within about four days unrefrigerated. It must not read as an ordinary wild bush, as fruit that appears days after the fire, or as a crop that keeps.
leaves.scenario: A burned pad and an unburned pad of the same ground and age; count scorch-fruit on each; let one ripen, have a colonist harvest it and a hungry colonist eat it; leave a ripe plant unpicked and a harvested stack in the open.
false_pass: scorch-fruit spawned by the test onto the burned pad
the unburned control is on non-Pyrelands ground, which refuses it for another reason
leaves.red: scorch-fruit grows on unburned ash as wild growth, or picked fruit keeps for weeks; or scorch-fruit appears only days after the front has passed

leaves.oracle_proposed: census of the live map: every wild plant and animal defName is in the manifest; grazer count above predator count; zero red errors in the generation window
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player on a fresh Pyrelands map finds only the biome's own wild plants (ember grass, quick grass, scorch-fruit) and only its fire-ecology cast of animals, with small grazers outnumbering big predators, and no error appears while it generates. It must not read as a desert or savanna roster with fire art on it.
leaves.scenario: Generate a fresh map on the composed mandrake.rm.biomes list; census every wild plant and animal by defName against the biome's manifest; tap the log through generation.
false_pass: the census reads the BiomeDef's lists instead of the map
an intruder is counted as ours because it carries a patched label
leaves.red: a donor plant or animal grows or wanders on the map, or big predators outnumber the grazers

leaves.oracle_proposed: captures read as burned ruins; footprint terrain is deep ash and loose-ash filth is present
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player who finds ruins on a fresh Pyrelands map sees them blackened and fire-scarred, with deep ash on their footprint and loose ash in them, so they warn what happens here. It must not read as pristine ruins on a burned plain.
leaves.scenario: Fresh map with ruins; capture each ruin at play zoom; read terrain and filth on its footprint.
false_pass: a ruin is stamped scorched only in its inspect text
leaves.red: ruins generate clean, on soil, with no ash in them

leaves.oracle_proposed: job reads carry-ember then drop; a fire appears at the drop cell beyond the front before the front reaches it; in the control no fire appears at that cell in the same window
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player watching a blaze sees a fire-hawk pick up a burning twig at the fire and a new fire start where it drops it, ahead of the blaze. It must not read as ordinary fire spread reaching that cell. Carry and drop are read as state, never watched live without him.
leaves.scenario: A grass pad with a fire at one end and no fire ahead (asserted), one fire-hawk; read the hawk's job and carried thing each tick window; control: the same pad and fire with no hawk.
false_pass: the drop cell lit by the fire's own spread
a fire spawned at the drop cell by the test
leaves.red: the hawk never carries a twig, or its drop starts no fire

leaves.oracle_proposed: live RM_FurnaceBeast body size 6, against the classic 3.2 when the giant switch's restore runs; status present beside the beast and absent away from it; the beast's room clearly hotter than the twin room after a few hours
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player sees the furnace-beast as a giant, standing far larger than any other animal on the map; a colonist standing in the open near it shows a readable warmth status that goes away when it walks off, and a closed room holding a furnace-beast grows clearly hotter than the same room without one. It must not read as a heater building, as ordinary body heat, or as a beast the size of a muffalo.
leaves.scenario: Read the live furnace-beast's body size and drawn size against the other animals; colonist beside a furnace-beast, then walked ten cells away; two identical closed rooms, one holding a furnace-beast; read status and room temperature each hour.
false_pass: the warmth status is applied by the test
the hot room is hot because of the burn outside
the size is read from the XML file, not the running game's def
leaves.red: the beast is ordinary-sized, no warmth status appears near it, or its room stays at the other room's temperature

leaves.oracle_proposed: burrowed status read while the front is on its cell, health unchanged after; in the control the same animal takes burn damage; the heat-hit ashwallow is not domed before the hit, domed with the burrow job within a few ticks of it, surfaced after the hold, and never domed with the dome switch off
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player sees an ashwallow, as the front reaches it, show a readable burrowed status and dive, and come up unharmed once the fire has passed; struck by heat it curls into its dome stance. It must not read as an animal the fire simply missed.
leaves.scenario: An ashwallow on a grass pad with a fire front driven over its cell; read its status and health before, during and after; control: the same with the burrow switch off. Separately, an ashwallow on a pad with no ground fire, struck once by a heat hit that lights nothing: read its dome state before, at once after and when the hold runs out; control: the same hit with the dome switch off.
false_pass: the fire never reached the animal's cell
the animal is healed by the test after the fire
the dome sprite is drawn all the time, or the animal simply lies down when hurt
leaves.red: the ashwallow burns like any grazer, or never shows a burrowed status, or a heat hit leaves it standing

leaves.oracle_proposed: herd centroid moves toward the two-day-old pad; in the control it shows no drift toward either pad
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player sees ullai herds drift to graze where the fire burned about two days ago, not to fresh ash or old grass. It must not read as a herd wandering at random that happens to pass a scar. (No north-star bar of its own: it hangs on the cast bar until the walk gains one.)
leaves.scenario: Two burned pads, one burned two days ago and one an hour ago, an ullai herd equidistant; read herd centroid each game hour for a day; control: no burn history.
false_pass: the herd is spawned on the scar
the herd's drift target is set by the test
leaves.red: the herd ignores the two-day-old burn, or goes to the fresh one

leaves.oracle_proposed: a blind reader told apart the three captures and from vanilla rain; lightning strikes counted under cinderfall; fire count falls and loose ash washes away under black rain
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player sees three skies each recognisable at a glance: ash fall dims the map and banks drifts, cinderfall is its own look and brings lightning, black rain falls visibly dark and puts fires out. It must not read as one weather renamed three times, or as ordinary blue-grey rain.
leaves.scenario: Force each weather in turn on the same map at noon; capture each at play zoom; a blind reader names them; read fires out under black rain.
false_pass: the weathers differ only in their def fields
the captures are taken at night so all read dark
leaves.red: cinderfall looks like ash fall, or black rain draws as blue-grey rain

leaves.oracle_proposed: no ordinary rain on the list; none chosen over the season
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.cannot_show: ordinary rain falling on a Pyrelands map
leaves.experience: The player never sees ordinary rain fall on a Pyrelands map; its only wet weather is black rain.
leaves.scenario: Read the biome's weather commonalities and the weathers chosen over a compressed season.
false_pass: the season ran with weather forced off
leaves.red: ordinary rain is on the biome's weather list or is ever chosen

leaves.oracle_proposed: no fire cell on the far side while the near side burns at the strip edge, in clear weather throughout; a near-side smoulder relight does not cross; an ember on paving lights nothing; in the no-strip control the far side burns; RM_FE_FirebreakLine absent from the def database
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player who paves a strip at least two cells wide of any non-flammable, plant-free vanilla floor round a field, in clear weather, sees the walking front stop at it and a smoulder relight lit on the near side stop at it too; an ember dropped on the paving lights nothing, though a fire-hawk can carry one up to six cells past the strip and start a fire there, which is the sprayer's job. The colony's defence is vanilla, with no mod firebreak floor and no chemfuel. It must not read as the ground fire jumping a two-cell paved strip, or as a special floor the mod requires.
leaves.scenario: Clear weather asserted and held; a grass bed on both sides of a two-cell flagstone strip; drive the front at it and keep it burning at the strip edge; let the near side die down and relight a smoulder on the near side next to the strip; drop a hawk ember on the paving; controls: the same bed with no strip burns through, and a hawk ember carried six cells past the strip lights the far side.
false_pass: the fire was put out by weather before it reached the strip
the strip is the old RM_FE_FirebreakLine floor
the relight is lit far from the strip so it never tests it
leaves.red: the front or a near-side smoulder relight crosses a two-cell paved strip, or the firebreak floor is still buildable

leaves.oracle_proposed: the probe reads a burned wet cell and a dry old cell differently, part by part; refuses when the ash field switch is off
leaves.experience: The tester reads, per cell, base fertility, the watered lift, the fresh-burn bonus and its age, and whether rain is on the cell.
leaves.scenario: Build a bridge read returning those four parts of a cell's fertility for a rectangle; refuse with a reason when the ash field is off.
false_pass: the probe returns the BiomeDef's base fertility for every cell
leaves.red: the probe is missing, so the compound ruling cannot be measured cell by cell

leaves.oracle_proposed: state digest before save equals after reload (fire cells, scar ages, fertility parts, fruit); the second pass yields fruit again; switches leave no leftovers; log clean
leaves.tier_reason: the breadth failure only shows on his full list in ordinary play with a mid-way reload, which no quicktest reproduces
leaves.experience: The player plays a fresh Pyrelands colony through about two weeks on the full list: watches the burn line cross, picks scorch-fruit from the scar, sows on a fresh burn and on watered ash, shelters with a furnace-beast through an ash fall, saves mid-way while the front is walking, reloads, and finds the front, the scars, their bonuses and the fruit exactly as they were.
leaves.scenario: Fresh map on his full list; save while the front walks and a fresh scar holds scorch-fruit; reload and compare front cells, scar ages, fertility parts and fruit; repeat the core action (let the line pass a second field and harvest again); then a second order: sow first and let the fire come to the crop, then harvest fruit; turn the Pyrelands mechanics switches off and on mid-game; a paved ring protects the colony throughout.
false_pass: the reload is from a save made before the front lit
the repeat runs on a fresh map
leaves.red: after the reload the front is gone, scars read old, or the burn bonus resets

leaves.oracle_proposed: thermal charge rises while the beast stands by live fire and falls once it is moved to cold ground; the beast takes no injury standing in fire or struck by flame; after a rest on grass, its bed cells burn; with furnace thermal switched off the charge stays flat and the bed never lights; an ullai in the same fire takes burns
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player watching a furnace-beast in the burn sees it walk into the fire, stand there untouched while the grass burns round it and glow brighter as it banks the heat, then leave the burn once it is full; after it has lain down to rest on grass, the ground it lay on is smouldering when it gets up. It must not read as a beast the fire happened to miss, or as a heater that never runs down, or as a bed fire the test lit.
leaves.scenario: A furnace-beast with low charge beside a grass pad with a live fire, and an ullai in the same fire; read charge, health and job each hour; move the charged beast to cold ground and read the charge falling; let it rest on a grass pad and read fire on its bed cells when it wakes; control: the same with furnace thermal switched off.
false_pass: the charge is set by the test rather than earned by the fire
the bed cells were lit by the burn line rather than by the beast
the beast stood beside the fire, never in it
leaves.red: the beast's charge never rises in the burn, it takes burns in fire, or its bed never smoulders

leaves.oracle_proposed: the sprayed path's fire cells go out and the colonist reaches the fruit, picks it and walks back with no burn injury; in the control without the sprayer the colonist either refuses to path through fire or comes back burned
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player who sends a colonist carrying the firefoam sprayer into a live burn for scorch-fruit sees the colonist foam a way through the fire, pick the fruit standing in the scar and come back out unburned. It must not read as the fire happening to die on its own, or as a colonist walking through fire unharmed with no sprayer.
leaves.scenario: A live burn in grass with ripe scorch-fruit in its scar, weather clear and fire still burning (asserted); a colonist with the sprayer ordered to harvest; read fire cells on the path, the colonist's path and health; control: the same with a colonist without the sprayer.
false_pass: the fire burned out before the colonist moved
the fruit was outside the fire, so no spray was needed
leaves.red: the sprayer does not put the fire out, or the colonist comes back burned

leaves.oracle_proposed: the sand cell yields 5 glass sand and turns to gravel, and the order is no longer offered on it; the deep-ash cell refuses the order
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player who orders a colonist to shovel a patch of Pyrelands sand gets five glass sand per cell, and the cell turns to gravel, so every sand patch is a finite deposit. It must not read as a dig order that works on any ground, or a sand cell that can be dug forever.
leaves.scenario: A colonist holding a shovel, a Pyrelands sand cell and a deep-ash cell (asserted by terrain read); designate both; read yield and terrain after; designate the dug cell again.
false_pass: the glass sand was spawned by the test
the non-sand control is a cell the colonist cannot reach
leaves.red: shovelling yields nothing, or the cell stays sand and can be dug again

leaves.oracle_proposed: with no campaign mod loaded the log is clean through a burn; a test listener attached to the hook receives one event per burn clock beat
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The tester running the biome alone sees the fire clock tick through a burn with nothing in the log about the rite hook, and sees a listener attached to the hook hear every beat, so a campaign mod can answer the fire without this mod depending on it. It must not read as a hook that is silent because it never fires.
leaves.scenario: Pyrelands loaded without PyrelandsMechanics, log tap open; let the fire clock tick through a burn; control: attach a test listener and count its events over the same burn.
false_pass: the hook is silent because the fire clock never ticked
the listener is counted from a different event
leaves.red: the hook logs errors with no listener, or never raises

leaves.oracle_proposed: the RM_Pyrelands BiomeDef description, as loaded, says the savanna was genetically engineered
leaves.experience: The player who reads the Pyrelands biome description on the world map learns that this grass savanna was genetically engineered and has burned for millennia. It must not read as a natural wildfire grassland.
leaves.scenario: Read the RM_Pyrelands description in Defs/BiomeDefs/Pyrelands.xml and in the offline def dump.
false_pass: the word appears only in a plant's description, not the biome's
leaves.red: the biome description never says the savanna was engineered

leaves.oracle_proposed: after a flamefang bite the colonist's hediffs hold RM_FlamefangVenom and its severity rises over the next hours; after a bite from a non-venomous predator of like size no RM_FlamefangVenom is present
leaves.tier_reason: a running Pyrelands map with the biome's clocks, which a dev quicktest colony on the minimal list plus mandrake.rm.biomes gives in ~90 s
leaves.experience: The player whose colonist is bitten by a flamefang sees flamefang venom appear on that colonist's health tab, smouldering worse over the following hours until treated or thrown off. It must not read as an ordinary bite wound, or as vanilla toxic buildup with a new name.
leaves.scenario: A colonist and a hostile flamefang on a cleared pad; let the flamefang land bites; read the colonist's hediffs and the venom's severity each hour; control: the same colonist bitten by a non-venomous predator of like size.
false_pass: the venom hediff is added by the test
any bite or melee hit applies the venom
leaves.red: a flamefang bite leaves only a wound, with no venom on the health tab
